chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Fadl, the freedman of Muhammad ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: 'I married a woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah), but it occurred to me that she had a husband, so I investigated that matter and found that she indeed had a husband.' He said: 'And why did you investigate?'

key_terms.فَفَتَّشْتُ: I investigated / I searched, referring to verifying the status of the woman's previous marriage.
key_terms.فَوَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِي: It occurred to me / I suspected, indicating the narrator's internal doubt or realization.
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Temporary marriage (mut'ah), a form of marriage in Shia jurisprudence with a specified duration.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on temporary marriage (mut'ah) if the woman already has a living husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the juristic principle that the validity of a temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) is contingent upon the woman being free from any existing marital bond, whether permanent or temporary. Imam al-Sadiq’s rhetorical question, 'Why did you investigate?', underscores that the presence of a prior husband acts as a legal impediment (*hijab*) to the new contract, a key distinction in Shia fiqh compared to Sunni schools which often restrict *mut'ah* to widows or divorcees. This narration serves as a primary evidence for the condition of *kafā'ah* regarding marital status in Shi'i temporary marriage contracts.
